action_items: Verify the z-index bump on the Landing navbar (z-10 → z-30) does not introduce regressions with any future overlays/modals on Landing.

(OUT-OF-SCOPE per request, just FYI) The onboarding modal that pops on first dashboard load is still hardcoded in French ("Bienvenue sur CodeForge AI", "Crée des applications…", "Suivant") even when the dashboard locale is e.g. Russian. Same for some UserMenu dropdown labels. Mentioned in the iter_27 brief as out of scope but worth tracking.
critical_code_review_comments: [FIXED] /app/frontend/src/pages/Landing.js — the <nav> wrapper had `relative z-10` and the hero <section> right below it ALSO has `relative z-10`. Each `relative` creates a new stacking context, so the LanguageToggle dropdown's `z-50` was scoped to the navbar's z-10 context and was visually drawn but click-intercepted by the hero section (elementFromPoint returned the hero <section>, so option clicks did nothing). Bumped navbar to `relative z-30` — fixes Landing language switching for all 12 languages.
Discover/Dashboard navbars are `z-20`/`z-50` already, which is why the same toggle worked there.
Translations: ES/DE/ZH/RU/HI/PT/NL/ZH-TW/BN/UR all wired correctly for l_* and d_* keys; FR+EN are full and the abridged 10 fall back gracefully where keys aren't overridden.

Discover lock blocker also catches clicks on tutorial card children that AREN'T marked `data-discover-allow`. Currently OK because the tutorial card itself wraps the prev/next buttons under a parent that has `data-discover-allow`. Worth a regression check if buttons are restructured.
describeApp / generationInProgress are FR/EN-only — confirmed in the brief as out-of-scope; rendering uses `t('describeApp') || 'Prompt'` fallback so no UI break.

rca_of_the_issue: ROOT CAUSE: stacking-context isolation. In Landing.js the <motion.nav> used `relative z-10`. The hero <section> immediately following it also used `relative z-10`. Both `position: relative` + `z-index` create new stacking contexts. The LanguageToggle dropdown's internal `z-50` only competes inside the navbar's z-10 context, so against sibling stacking contexts at the same outer level (the hero section, declared LATER in source order) it loses on tie-breaking and the hero section is painted on top in the hit-test layer. Visually the dropdown looked open and rendered above the page, but document.elementFromPoint(x,y) at any option's center returned the <section> — confirmed via in-page evaluate. Clicking via Playwright (which uses real hit testing) therefore landed on the section, not the option, so setLanguage() was never invoked and localStorage stayed unchanged. REPRO STEPS: (1) load /, (2) click [data-testid=language-toggle] → dropdown visible, (3) click [data-testid=language-option-es] with force=true → no language change, H1 still English, localStorage codeforge_language unchanged. FIX APPLIED: change navbar wrapper from `relative z-10` to `relative z-30` so its internal `z-50` dropdown wins against the hero section's z-10 stacking context. Verified: 5/5 sampled languages (es, de, zh, ru, hi) now switch H1 + nav-discover + signup button correctly on Landing.
